text: 反对他的主要是两位朋友：一位是去哈佛升学、最坚定的反对者梅光迪，另一位是同在康乃尔、写诗嘲笑过他的任鸿隽。争的是白话能不能用来写文学。到1916年夏天，朋友们已承认白话可以写小说、演说，唯独不肯承认它能作诗，反对者已经退到只剩一处：诗。胡适采取的办法，是先把朋友们反对的理由排个队：一是从来没有诗人用俗语俗字作过诗，他自己也只找到一首、甚至只是一首中的几句是用白话写的；二是他们更能言之成理的一条，从来没有中国作家认真着实用白话作诗。按他自己的说法，这许多严肃的讨论都只源于一首送别诗引起的小小偶然事件；让他下定决心不写旧诗、要写就用活的语言来写的，则是又一件偶然发生的小事——湖上那场险事。

His chief opponents were two friends: Mei Guangdi, bound for Harvard and his most determined opponent, and Ren Hongjun, also at Cornell, who had mocked him in verse. The quarrel was over whether the vernacular could serve literature. By the summer of 1916 his friends granted that it would do for fiction and speeches, but not for poetry. Poetry was the last fortress. Hu's tactic was first to set out his friends' objections in order. First, no poet had ever written verse in colloquial words; he himself could find only one poem, perhaps only a few lines of one, written in the vernacular. Second, and more persuasive, no Chinese writer had ever seriously written poetry in the vernacular. In his own telling, all the serious discussion grew out of a small accident set off by a farewell poem; what made him resolve to stop writing old-style verse and write only in the living language was another small accident, the incident on the lake.
